analysis.title: US GDP forecasts revised up on robust domestic demand
key_insights: ANZ revised up its US growth forecasts after Q3 GDP of 3.4% saar: average 2.4% y/y this year, 2.3% in 2027 and 2.2% in 2028.

ANZ does not expect the Democrats' clean sweep of Congress to materially affect growth. Legislation to curb AI investment would face a presidential veto, and the debt ceiling is expected to be raised with few curbs on federal spending over the next two years.
Private non-residential investment contributed 1.8% to Q3 GDP growth, and investment in information processing equipment accounted for half of that.
AI investment is estimated to rise from around USD0.8trn this year to USD1.2trn in 2027 and grow again in 2028, making it a major contributor to GDP over the forecast horizon.
The capex cycle is broadening beyond AI: industrial equipment investment contributed about 0.3% to GDP growth in both Q2 and Q3.
Consumption rose 3.8% saar over the past two quarters. The top 20% of households account for about 40% of consumer spending, supported by wealth effects and high incomes.

Affordability is a constraint for most households: in 2025 consumers spent 46.9% of income on housing and food, the highest share in 15 years. Low unemployment and low labour force attrition keep lower and median-income households spending.

Real private final sales to domestic purchasers rose 4.9% saar in Q3, up from 4.6% in Q2, against a 2.3% average over the 20 years before Covid. ANZ attributes the outperformance mainly to the AI super-cycle.
Strong domestic demand raises the risk that sticky inflation persists longer, which is a contributing factor to ANZ's expectation of additional monetary tightening.

risk_factors: Sticky inflation may persist longer because of strong domestic demand, which raises the risk of further monetary tightening.
Affordability constraints and rising income inequality weigh on lower and median-income households.
Growth depends heavily on AI investment and on wealth effects concentrated in the top 20% of households.
geopolitical: Democrats won a clean sweep of Congress, which ANZ does not expect to materially change growth momentum.
A presidential veto would block legislation to curb AI investment.
The debt ceiling is expected to be increased with few curbs on aggregate federal spending over the next two years.
